title: census.py groups and brief split the phase-2 rows into owner groups and print each group's filled brief with its review passages and cited facts
goal: census.py groups LOG prints, as JSON, the phase-2 rows grouped by the domain of the files citing them with the skill's owner rule (a source cited in two groups goes to the group with most of its citations, its other files listed as foreign), each group with its rows, owned files, foreign files and queue size, deterministic for a given log and tree; census.py brief LOG --group G prints that group's phase-2 brief as the skill words it today, filled in: the rows with id, url, bucket, evidence and used_in, each row's citing facts as rag.py src --cited gives them (path:line and text), the factdiff review items inline for rows whose evidence names factdiff.py review, the read command for each other row (git show and git diff for a pinned file, the fetch route for a page), and the result JSON shape, so the reader needs no lookup call to start; the brief stays under a size bound the command states and splits a group over it into numbered parts.

gates.question: What size bound does one brief part keep, and what happens to a source whose own block is over it? (recommended: 30000 characters, 7500 tokens at 4 characters a token, so the entra dry run's 43 review items, 24212 characters, fit one part; a source is one outcome, so it is never split)
options: 30000 characters a part; a source alone over it is a part of its own
30000 characters a part; a source over it has its citing lines split across parts
10000 characters a part; a source alone over it is a part of its own
gates.recommendation: 30000 characters a part; a source alone over it is a part of its own
gates.answer: 30000 characters a part; a source alone over it is a part of its own

gates.question: How does groups count a source's citations to find its owner group, break a tie and place a row no file names? (recommended: citing lines in the tree, a ledger or root-level file counting for no domain; a tie to the first domain by name; a row no line names falls back to the files of its log used_in, else the group _uncited)
options: citing lines in the tree; tie to the first domain by name; fall back to used_in, else _uncited
citing files, not lines; tie to the first domain by name; fall back to used_in, else _uncited
citing lines in the tree; tie to the domain with most rows already; no used_in fallback
gates.recommendation: citing lines in the tree; tie to the first domain by name; fall back to used_in, else _uncited
gates.answer: citing lines in the tree; tie to the first domain by name; fall back to used_in, else _uncited

gates.question: Does brief read the fact diff review passages offline (cache, snapshot, anchor quote; no Wayback capture, no page fetch) like the queue summary, or online like factdiff.py review? (recommended: offline, so the brief holds what the summary's reading cost counted and the command stays free of the network)
options: offline: the passages the queue summary counts; a passage only the network could give prints as -
online by default, as factdiff.py review does
offline by default, an --online flag adds Wayback captures and page fetches
gates.recommendation: offline: the passages the queue summary counts; a passage only the network could give prints as -
gates.answer: offline: the passages the queue summary counts; a passage only the network could give prints as -

gates.question: Which citing lines does a row's brief block list? (recommended: the lines of the domain files, a front matter sources: line named without its id list, and no line of a ledger such as _answers.md, _gaps.md or _conflicts.md, which the orchestrator handles)
options: domain files' lines with their text; a front matter sources: line named without its list; no ledger lines
every line rag.py src --cited gives, ledger lines and front matter lists included
domain files' lines only, front matter lines left out too
gates.recommendation: domain files' lines with their text; a front matter sources: line named without its list; no ledger lines
gates.answer: domain files' lines with their text; a front matter sources: line named without its list; no ledger lines

gates.question: How does the caller pick one numbered part of a group's brief? (recommended: brief LOG --group G --part N, N from 1, default 1, and groups prints each group's number of parts)
options: --part N on brief, default 1; parts count in the groups output
each part its own group name such as agents-2, no --part flag
brief prints every part in one output, separated by a marker line
gates.recommendation: --part N on brief, default 1; parts count in the groups output
gates.answer: --part N on brief, default 1; parts count in the groups output
